block.title: Base block 1: aerobic base and first loaded strength
block.content:
## goals

Under 100 kg and weight that stays off, from 129.2 kg. Complete the Alpe du Zwift within 12 weeks at any time, which the model puts at about 3h38m on current numbers.

The block's own job is narrower: build an aerobic base that does not exist yet, and put the first load through a lower body that has never had any. Everything else follows those two.

## constraints

Seeded as safety facts and repeated here because the document is what gets read when a session is written. L5-S1 repair November 2025, recovery complete, morning stiffness of 3.5 to 4 out of 5 is his normal. No loaded hip hinge until week 8. No side planks. No barbell work of any kind, and no barbell exists in the gym anyway. Cannot pedal standing.

## physiology

FTP 115 W from the ramp test of 27 July, threshold heart rate 152, observed max 169. Endurance is 64 to 86 W and 123 to 135 bpm. Easy means under 135 bpm, target 130, and heart rate wins any argument with the power number.

Benchmark #1 on 1 August: 84.4 W at 130.3 bpm over 45 minutes, with power falling 19.3 percent from the first third to the last while heart rate held. Whole ride 98.4 percent Z1 and Z2. That is measurement zero and it repeats every four weeks; next around 29 August.

## plan

Six days, one genuine rest day on Thursday. Roughly 3 hours a week on the bike and not above 4 for now.

Monday easy endurance. Tuesday gym A, lower emphasis, physio core work before the strength block because it got sacrificed when it was placed last. Wednesday the quality bike session, sweet spot from week 2. Thursday rest. Friday gym B, upper emphasis. Saturday the long easy ride, or the benchmark every fourth week. Sunday golf or rest, his choice.

Progression rules: two reps in reserve on everything for the first four weeks and no failure, add reps before load, one progression at a time and never gym load and ride volume in the same week, and if stiffness rises after two consecutive sessions regress that one movement for a week.

Routes for easy rides are flat, Tempus Fugit or Tick Tock. His July variability index averaged 1.14 against a target under 1.05, and the Paris and France routes force surges. Route completion after a workout ends is encouraged at the same heart rate or lower, never higher; the moment ERG releases is the highest risk drift point in a session.

## review
block.reason: seeded from coaching-state.md v1.1.0, the block already running since 27 July 2026

notes.body: Context around the constraints that cannot live in the constraint lists themselves, because SAFE-06 parses those phrase by phrase against the movement vocabulary. Morning stiffness of 3.5 to 4 out of 5 on waking is his normal and clears by mid-morning; a rise above that baseline is the signal, not the absolute number. The physio course ended months ago and was focused entirely on the back, so it never reached lower body loading and the first loaded lower body work of his life was 28 July 2026. Side planks are out of the programme: shoulder pain at bodyweight load in that movement only, with no pain in any other movement including all pressing. Not recorded as a movement restriction, deliberately, because the phrase resolves against two trunk patterns and excluding either would ban front planks or Pallof presses, which are in every session and are precisely what the repaired disc wants. Do not prescribe side planks; do keep the rest of the trunk work. He cannot pedal while standing, because the Zwift Ride frame is fixed and does not sway; standing breaks are stop pedalling, stand 15 to 20 seconds, sit back down, taken in interval recoveries rather than mid-interval and kept identical on benchmark rides.

Baseline block, 8 to 27 July 2026. Thirteen rides, 7.9 hours actual riding, about 3 hours a week. Eighty one percent of that time was tempo or harder, which held under every plausible HRmax assumption from 172 to 190. The cause was a broken anchor rather than poor discipline: Zwift's FTP field read 146 W, which is above his best 5 minute power and physiologically impossible, so Zwift's Zone 2 displayed as 82 to 110 W and he rode it faithfully. Against a real threshold near 115 W that band is tempo. Ramp test on 27 July set FTP at 115 W, threshold heart rate 152, observed max 169.

Benchmark #1, Tempus Fugit, 45 minute free ride block with heart rate pinned at 130, fasted plus coffee, two fans and electrolytes. Average 84.4 W at 130.3 bpm, 0.648 W per bpm, 82 rpm, 0.4 percent coasting. First 15 minutes 95.5 W, middle 80.7 W, last 77.1 W: a 19.3 percent power drop with heart rate flat. Whole ride 98.4 percent Z1 and Z2. Morning weight 129.2 kg, Whoop 69 percent recovery on 9h08 sleep. Do not read the first five minutes at 106.7 W as his sustainable ability; the 77 W at the end is closer to what his aerobic system currently supports. This is measurement zero and repeats every four weeks.

The heat versus aerobic base question is settled, in favour of aerobic base. July rides drifted about 8 bpm at matched power across three long rides, and the competing explanations were Dubai heat at 129 kg with one fan, or an absent aerobic base. Benchmark #1 ran the full cooling and hydration protocol at a low heart rate, so heat load should have been minimal, and the decoupling was still about 20 percent against under 5 percent for a well trained rider. It is aerobic base. That is the most trainable thing he has and it should move faster than FTP does.

Cycling will not drive the weight loss and he has been told so. Total mechanical work across the thirteen July rides was 2,530 kJ, about 984 kcal a week or 140 kcal a day. Diet is doing roughly 95 percent of the deficit. Intake target is 2,350 kcal with 175 g protein, 255 g carbohydrate, 70 g fat and 35 g fibre, against an estimated maintenance of 2,750 to 3,050 which cannot be resolved by equations. The adjustment rule is to log at 2,350 for three weeks and read the 7 day rolling average: under 0.4 kg a week drop to 2,150, over 0.8 raise to 2,550, and do not adjust before three weeks. Do not eat back exercise calories. The weekly takeaway stays, because eliminating enjoyed food predicts relapse.

Body composition is estimated and not measured: roughly 40.6 percent fat and 76.6 kg fat free mass, from Deurenberg on BMI. Every macro figure downstream of that is only as good as the estimate, and a DEXA or a decent bioimpedance reading would tighten all of them. The protein target of 175 g is 2.3 g per kg of that estimated fat free mass. If the estimate moves, the protein target moves with it.

Week 1 executed, 27 July to 1 August. Monday ramp test, FTP 115 W. Tuesday gym A, the first loaded lower body work of his life; he went close to failure against a two-reps-in-reserve instruction, skipped step ups for want of a platform and side planks for shoulder pain, and reported back 2.5 out of 5 that evening which cleared normally by morning. Wednesday golf. Thursday endurance 60, 64 W at 124 bpm average and 132 max, with zero minutes above 135, the first genuine endurance ride in the dataset. Friday gym B, strain 9.5 against a typical 11.4, RPE 7, loads too light at 8 kg total on the presses. Saturday Benchmark #1. The gym A session at 119 bpm average was cardiovascularly easier than every single July bike ride, which is an independent confirmation of the intensity misallocation arriving from a different direction.

Open threads as of 2 August. Fourteen consecutive days of logged food including the bad days has not started and is the single biggest open item, because it blocks the nutrition review due around 24 August. Baseline bloods and the sleep-disordered-breathing conversation are both outstanding. Cleat position was set fully rearward on 2 August and is being assessed through week 2. The saddle nose was dropped slightly on 1 August and nothing else on the saddle should change until that trial is read. Gym B working loads are to be found on Friday 7 August, expect 8 to 12 kg a hand. A 20 minute test to cross check FTP is due at week 5, the next ramp test at week 12, Benchmark #2 around 29 August, and the loaded hip hinge is revisited at week 8. Hell of the North was deferred from 8 to 15 August because week 2 already carries first intensity, a 25 percent jump in long ride duration, and new shoes; one progression at a time.
